course_name_original: Dirección y Gestión de Centros de Servicios y Factorías de Software
course_name_en: Direction and Management of Service Centers and Software Factories
prerequisites: Competences and knowledge from courses related to 'Direction and Management of Technology-Based Companies' and 'ICT Products and Services'
Knowledge of computer infrastructure (hardware and software)
Ability to read and understand documentation written in English

learning_outcomes.text: Know the structure of a service center and its operation.
Know the technical-economic direction and management techniques of service centers.
Know the different models of a software factory and its operation.
Know the technical-economic direction and management techniques of software factories.
Know business continuity techniques in service centers.

syllabus_topics: Logical and physical structure of a service center.
Administration, operation, and maintenance of a service center.
Business continuity and disaster recovery in a service center.
Energy efficiency in a service center.
Productivity management and production processes in software factories
Financial management of software factories. Acquisition/contracting and commercialization models.
Design of the logical and physical structure of a service center.
Design of a contingency plan for a service center.
Elaboration of a production plan, work organization, and sizing for a software factory.

assessment_methods.method: Practical Work 1 (P1) - Group work during the service centers block
Practical Work 2 (P2) - Group work at the end of the service centers block
Practical Work 3 (P3) - Group work after the software factories block
Theoretical Exam (T1) - Written test at the end of the course

assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, a minimum grade of 5/10 is required for both the practical and theoretical blocks. The practical block grade is calculated as (0.25*P1) + (0.25*P2) + (0.5*P3), and the theoretical block grade is T1. The final ordinary grade is (0.8*Practicals) + (0.2*Theory) if minimums are met; otherwise, it is the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. Group work can only be submitted in the ordinary examination. For extraordinary examination, if the practical part was approved in the ordinary call with at least 5/10, that grade is retained; otherwise, it is 0. A new in-person knowledge test must be passed with at least 5/10. The final extraordinary grade is (0.4*Practicals) + (0.6*Theory). If the practical part was not approved in the ordinary call, the maximum possible grade in the extraordinary call is 6.
